  "text": "The constable shoved the key through the window. It struck the table and spun to a stop beside the lantern.

“Lock it,” he gasped.

Ada picked it up. The iron was warm. Across its bow, five notches had been cut: three close together, then two.

The hatch bucked. A splinter flew from the oak bar and struck Venn’s wife on the cheek. She did not seem to feel it. She was watching the empty boat drift past the piling.

“There was no man in it when I went out,” the constable said.

Elias stopped pulling the rope. Its far end slipped from the bank into the river.

Mara pointed at a small brass plate set into the floor beside the stove. Ada had taken it for part of the hearth until she saw the keyhole. She knelt and fitted the key into it.

Below the hatch, something began to knock. Three blows. Two.

“Don’t answer,” Elias’s brother whispered.

Ada turned the key. A bolt shot across beneath the floor, and the hatch fell still. From outside came a heavy splash. Everyone looked toward the window, but the boat had passed beyond it.

Then the knocking sounded from the brass plate, directly under Ada’s hand.

She backed away. The key remained upright in the lock, trembling. Water seeped around the plate’s edges and spread across the boards toward the stove.

Venn’s wife took a step back. In the lanternlight, a second set of wet footprints appeared beside hers. No one stood in them."
